questions.q: Which description fits ARM processors?
options: 8-bit CISC chips with high power consumption
32-bit RISC cores with low power consumption
questions.exp: ARM cores are low-power RISC designs that dominate mobile phones and embedded devices.

questions.q: A microcontroller differs from a microprocessor mainly because a microcontroller integrates on one chip
options: CPU along with RAM, ROM, timers and I/O ports
questions.exp: A microcontroller is a computer on a chip: CPU plus memory and peripherals, whereas a microprocessor is essentially only the CPU.

questions.q: Which timer mode of the 8051 is the 8-bit auto-reload mode?
questions.exp: Mode 2 uses TLx as an 8-bit counter that is reloaded from THx on every overflow.

questions.q: In an 8085 program, MVI A,0FFH is followed by INR A (CY was 0 before). The Zero and Carry flags are
questions.exp: FFH + 1 = 00H so Z = 1; INR does not affect the carry flag, so CY stays 0.

questions.q: Which 8051 instruction reads a byte from external data memory?
questions.exp: MOVX accesses external data memory; MOVC reads code memory and MOV A,@R1 accesses internal RAM.

questions.q: Which interrupt has the highest default priority in the 8051?
questions.exp: The default order is INT0, Timer 0, INT1, Timer 1, Serial.

questions.q: Which 8085 instruction loads the accumulator from a memory location whose 16-bit address is given directly in the instruction?
questions.exp: LDA addr (direct addressing, 3 bytes) copies the byte at the given address into A.

questions.q: A UART in a microcontroller is used for
questions.exp: The Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter sends and receives serial frames with start and stop bits and no shared clock.

questions.q: An 8-bit ADC has a reference of 2.56 V. For an input of 1.00 V the digital output (in decimal) is
The interrupt vector table of the 8086 occupies
questions.exp: There are 256 interrupt types, each with a 4-byte vector (IP, CS), giving 1 KB from 00000H to 003FFH.

questions.q: An 8-bit ADC in a microcontroller uses a 5 V reference. The number of distinct digital output codes is
questions.exp: An n-bit ADC has 2^n codes: 2^8 = 256, so each step is about 5/256 = 19.5 mV.

questions.q: Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) in a microcontroller is commonly used to
options: control motor speed or LED brightness
questions.exp: Varying the duty cycle of a fixed-frequency pulse varies the average power delivered to a motor or LED.

questions.q: The instruction MOV AX,[BX+SI+08H] in the 8086 uses which addressing mode?
questions.exp: A base register (BX), an index register (SI) and an 8-bit displacement are all added, which is based indexed addressing with displacement.

questions.q:
Statement I: In the 8085 the stack pointer is a 16-bit register.
Statement II: In the 8085 the stack grows towards lower memory addresses.
Which is correct?
questions.exp: SP is 16 bits wide and PUSH decrements it by 2, so the stack grows downward.

questions.q: What is the vector address of RST 6.5 in the 8085?
questions.exp: Vectors: TRAP 0024H, RST 5.5 002CH, RST 6.5 0034H, RST 7.5 003CH.

questions.q: In an 8085 program A = 38H (BCD) and B = 45H (BCD). After ADD B followed by DAA the accumulator holds
questions.exp: 38H + 45H = 7DH; low nibble D > 9 so DAA adds 06H giving 83H, which is the BCD sum 38 + 45 = 83.

questions.q: Timer 1 of the 8051 is used in Mode 2 to overflow after 100 pulses. The value loaded in TH1 is
Which port of the 8051 microcontroller needs external pull-up resistors when used as a general-purpose I/O port?
questions.exp: Port 0 has open-drain outputs, so external pull-ups are needed for ordinary I/O use.

questions.q: The speed of a microprocessor is mainly specified by its
questions.exp: The clock frequency (MHz/GHz) sets how fast instructions execute; bus widths determine addressing range and data width instead.

questions.q: In an 8086, AL = 7FH, BL = 01H and ADD AL,BL is executed. Which flag outcome is correct?
questions.exp: 7FH + 01H = 80H: no unsigned carry (CF = 0), but two positive numbers give a negative result so OF = 1 and SF = 1.

questions.q: In a hard real-time embedded system
options: a missed deadline only slightly degrades quality
a missed deadline can be a system failure
questions.exp: Hard real-time systems must meet deadlines absolutely; missing one is treated as failure (e.g. airbag control).

questions.q: After a reset the program counter of the 8085 contains
questions.exp: Reset clears the program counter, so execution starts from 0000H.

questions.q: An 8051 executes MOV A,#3CH then SWAP A then ADD A,#05H. The accumulator contains
questions.exp: SWAP exchanges nibbles: 3CH becomes C3H; adding 05H gives C8H.

questions.q: The serial I/O lines of the 8085 are
questions.exp: SID (serial input data) and SOD (serial output data) are used with the RIM and SIM instructions.

questions.q: Which 8086 instruction reads a byte from port 0F8H directly into AL?
questions.exp: IN AL,port8 reads from an I/O port addressed directly by an 8-bit number.

questions.q: Which pin of the 8051 must be connected to logic 1 to execute programs from the internal ROM?
questions.exp: EA (External Access) = 1 makes the 8051 fetch from internal code memory (below 1000H); EA = 0 forces external memory.

questions.q: An 8051 runs from a 12 MHz crystal. Timer 1 in Mode 1 is to give a 1 ms delay. The value to load in TH1:TL1 is
questions.exp: Machine cycle = 1 microsecond, so 1000 counts are needed: 65536 - 1000 = 64536 = FC18H.

questions.q: An interrupt service routine (ISR) is
options: a routine executed when an interrupt occurs, ending with a return-from-interrupt instruction
a routine that runs only at power-on
a table that stores all interrupt vectors
a hardware line that carries the interrupt request
questions.exp: On an interrupt the CPU saves the PC, jumps to the ISR, and returns to the interrupted program at the end of the ISR.

questions.q: In the 8085 the ALE signal is used to
options: latch the lower address byte from the multiplexed AD0-AD7 lines
questions.exp: ALE goes high at the start of a machine cycle so an external latch (e.g. 74LS373) can capture A0-A7.

questions.q: Which interrupt of the 8085 has the highest priority?
questions.exp: TRAP is non-maskable and has the highest priority, followed by RST 7.5, 6.5, 5.5 and INTR.

questions.q: What is the bit address of bit 3 of the byte at address 28H in the 8051 bit-addressable RAM?
questions.exp: Byte 20H holds bits 00H-07H, so byte 28H starts at 40H; bit 3 is 43H.

questions.q: What is the interrupt vector (ROM) address of the Timer 1 overflow interrupt in the 8051?
questions.exp: 8051 vectors: INT0 0003H, Timer 0 000BH, INT1 0013H, Timer 1 001BH, Serial 0023H.

questions.q: Which 8085 instruction is used to mask the RST 5.5, 6.5 and 7.5 interrupts selectively?
questions.exp: SIM (Set Interrupt Mask) uses the accumulator bits to set or reset the individual RST mask bits; RIM only reads them.

questions.q: An 8085 system uses 8K x 8 memory chips with a 3-to-8 decoder driven by A15, A14, A13. The chip selected when A15 A14 A13 = 010 occupies addresses
questions.exp: 010 followed by 13 address bits spans 0100 0000 0000 0000 to 0101 1111 1111 1111, i.e. 4000H-5FFFH.

questions.q: Which pair correctly gives (data bus width, address bus width) of the 8086?
questions.exp: The 8086 has a 16-bit data bus (AD0-AD15) and 20 address lines.

questions.q: In an 8085 program, MVI A,45H is followed by ADI 3BH. What is the content of A and the Carry flag after ADI?
questions.exp: 45H + 3BH = 80H, which fits in 8 bits, so no carry is generated (CY = 0).

questions.q: In an 8085 program A = 30H and B = 40H and CMP B is executed. The flags are
questions.exp: CMP subtracts B from A without storing: A < B so a borrow occurs (CY = 1) and the result is non-zero (Z = 0).

questions.q: Which is generally the best choice for a low-cost, dedicated control task such as a TV remote controller?
options: Pentium-class processor running a full OS
questions.exp: A small 8-bit microcontroller with on-chip memory and I/O is cheap, low power and sufficient for such tasks.

questions.q: The word length of an 8-bit microprocessor means
options: it processes 8 bits of data at a time
questions.exp: The word length equals the width of the ALU and data bus, i.e. the data processed in one operation.

questions.q: The Intel 8086 is a
questions.exp: The 8086 is a 16-bit microprocessor with a 16-bit data bus and 20 address lines.

questions.q: In a microcontroller-based temperature measurement system the ADC is used to
options: convert digital values to analog voltages
convert the analog sensor voltage into a digital number
questions.exp: An analog-to-digital converter digitises the sensor output so the CPU can process it.

questions.q: After reset the 8086 begins executing instructions at physical address
questions.exp: On reset CS = FFFFH and IP = 0000H, so the physical address is FFFF0H.

questions.q: The 8051 uses which type of memory architecture?
questions.exp: The 8051 has separate address spaces for program (code) memory and data memory, which is the Harvard architecture.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The 8086 can fetch the next instruction while the current one is being executed.
Reason (R): The Bus Interface Unit and the Execution Unit work independently using an instruction queue.
options: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: The BIU pre-fetches instructions into the queue while the EU executes, which is exactly what produces the overlap.

questions.q: How many flags are present in the flag register of the 8085 microprocessor?
questions.exp: The 8085 has five flags: Sign, Zero, Auxiliary Carry, Parity and Carry.

questions.q: How many 16-bit timer/counters are available in the standard 8051?
questions.exp: The 8051 has Timer 0 and Timer 1; the 8052 adds Timer 2.

questions.q: Which of the following is a RISC-based 8-bit microcontroller family?
questions.exp: AVR and PIC are 8-bit RISC microcontrollers; the 8085, 8086 and Z80 are CISC microprocessors.

questions.q: Which of the following is a typical embedded application of a microcontroller?
questions.exp: A washing machine controller is a dedicated, low-cost control task, which is what microcontrollers are designed for.

questions.q: In an 8051 program, A = 50H and B = 04H and MUL AB is executed. The result is
questions.exp: 80 x 4 = 320 = 0140H; low byte 40H goes to A, high byte 01H to B, and OV = 1 because the product exceeds 255.

questions.q: Which of the 8085 interrupts is a non-vectored interrupt, i.e. the interrupting device must supply the instruction/vector?
questions.exp: INTR is non-vectored; the external device places an RST or CALL opcode on the data bus in response to INTA. The others have fixed vector addresses.

questions.q: The 8086 has 20 address lines. Its physical memory space is therefore
In an 8086, DS = 1234H and the offset is 0010H. The physical address is
Which statement about memory-mapped I/O is correct?
options: It uses only the IN and OUT instructions
The number of ports is limited to 256
I/O devices are treated like memory locations, so memory-reference instructions can be used on them
It does not reduce the memory space available for memory
questions.exp: In memory-mapped I/O devices share the memory address space, so any memory instruction (MOV, ADD, etc.) can access them, at the cost of memory space.

questions.q: Which serial interface uses a shared clock line (synchronous transfer)?
questions.exp: SPI (and I2C) use a clock line generated by the master, whereas UART/RS-232 are asynchronous with start and stop bits.

questions.q: The accumulator of an 8085 holds 82H and the instruction RLC is executed. The accumulator and Carry flag become
questions.exp: 82H = 1000 0010. Rotating left, bit 7 (1) goes to CY and into bit 0, giving 0000 0101 = 05H with CY = 1.

questions.q: Which serial bus uses only two lines called SDA and SCL?
questions.exp: The Inter-Integrated Circuit bus uses a serial data line (SDA) and a serial clock line (SCL).

questions.q: The 8051 serial port in Mode 1 transmits a frame consisting of
options: 9 data bits and no stop bit
questions.exp: Mode 1 is the 8-bit UART with variable baud rate and a 10-bit frame.

questions.q: Which of the following 8085 instructions does NOT affect any flag?
questions.exp: INX (16-bit increment) leaves all flags unchanged, whereas ADD, INR and ANA modify flags.

questions.q: Which memory in a microcontroller system loses its contents when power is removed?
questions.exp: RAM is volatile; Flash, EEPROM and ROM are non-volatile and hold the firmware.

questions.q: In the 8085, SP = 2000H and PUSH B is executed. What is the new SP and where is register C stored?
questions.exp: PUSH stores B at SP-1 = 1FFFH and C at SP-2 = 1FFEH, then SP becomes 1FFEH.

questions.q: The internal data RAM of the 8051 is
questions.exp: The 8051 has 128 bytes of on-chip data RAM (the 8052 has 256 bytes).

questions.q: Which of the following is a control flag in the 8086 flag register?
questions.exp: The control flags of the 8086 are TF, IF and DF; ZF, CF and AF are status flags.

questions.q: An 8085 system uses a 6 MHz crystal. How long does a NOP instruction (4 T-states) take?
questions.exp: The 8085 divides the crystal frequency by 2, giving a 3 MHz clock (T = 0.333 microseconds); 4 T-states = 1.333 microseconds.

questions.q: In a microcontroller, general-purpose I/O (GPIO) pins can be
options: configured as inputs or outputs by software
questions.exp: GPIO pins have direction registers so each pin can be programmed to read a switch (input) or drive an LED (output).

questions.q: A microprocessor with 16 address lines can directly address a memory of
questions.exp: 2^16 = 65,536 locations = 64 KB.

questions.q: To transfer a 16-bit word starting at an even address, the 8086 makes BHE and A0 respectively
questions.exp: BHE = 0 enables the upper half of the data bus and A0 = 0 enables the lower half, so both bytes transfer in one cycle.

questions.q: Compared with a general-purpose microprocessor, a microcontroller typically has
options: higher clock speed and large external memory support only
an instruction set designed mainly for number crunching
lower cost and power with bit-oriented instructions for control tasks
questions.exp: Microcontrollers target dedicated control with on-chip peripherals and bit-manipulation instructions at low cost and power.

questions.q: Which bus of a microprocessor system is bidirectional?
questions.exp: Data travels both to and from the CPU on the data bus, while the address bus is unidirectional (CPU to memory/I/O).

questions.q: Which flag in the 8051 PSW reflects the parity of the accumulator?
questions.exp: The P flag (PSW.0) is set when the accumulator contains an odd number of 1 bits.

questions.q: In the 8086, CS = 2000H and IP = 0150H. What is the physical address of the next instruction?
questions.exp: Physical address = CS x 16 + IP = 20000H + 0150H = 20150H.

questions.q: The stack of a microprocessor works on which principle?
questions.exp: PUSH stores data on top of the stack and POP removes the most recently pushed item first.

questions.q: In an 8086 with SS = 3000H and SP = 0100H, PUSH AX is executed. At which physical address is AH stored?
questions.exp: SP becomes 00FEH; the high byte AH is stored at SP+1 = 00FFH (physical 300FFH) and AL at 300FEH.

questions.q: The Arduino Uno board is based on which microcontroller?
questions.exp: The Arduino Uno uses the 8-bit Atmel/Microchip AVR ATmega328P running at 16 MHz.

questions.q: Match the devices: (i) 8255 (ii) 8253 (iii) 8259 (iv) 8279 with (a) programmable interval timer (b) programmable peripheral interface (c) keyboard/display controller (d) programmable interrupt controller.
questions.exp: 8255 is the PPI, 8253 the timer, 8259 the interrupt controller and 8279 the keyboard/display interface.

questions.q: The 8086 string instruction MOVSB copies a byte
questions.exp: MOVSB copies the byte at DS:SI to ES:DI and then adjusts SI and DI according to DF.

questions.q: In the 8051 PSW, RS1 RS0 = 1 0 selects the register bank located at
questions.exp: Bank 0 = 00H-07H, bank 1 = 08H-0FH, bank 2 = 10H-17H, bank 3 = 18H-1FH; RS1 RS0 = 10 selects bank 2.

questions.q: A DAC connected to a microcontroller port is used to
options: produce an analog voltage (for example a waveform) from digital values
questions.exp: A DAC converts the digital numbers written by the MCU into an analog voltage, e.g. to synthesise a sine wave or audio.

questions.q: Which register of a microprocessor holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched?
questions.exp: The program counter (IP in the 8086) points to the next instruction and is updated after each fetch.

questions.q: The bit-addressable area of the 8051 internal RAM lies at addresses
questions.exp: 16 bytes from 20H to 2FH give 128 individually addressable bits (00H-7FH).

questions.q: What is the size of the instruction prefetch queue of the 8086?
questions.exp: The 8086 has a 6-byte queue (the 8088 has a 4-byte queue).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the standard 8051?
questions.exp: The standard 8051 has no on-chip ADC; one must be interfaced externally.

questions.q: In the I/O-mapped I/O scheme of the 8085, how many input ports can be addressed?
questions.exp: IN and OUT instructions carry an 8-bit port address, so 2^8 = 256 input ports (and 256 output ports) are possible.

questions.q: The block of a microprocessor that decodes instructions and generates the timing and control signals is the
questions.exp: The control unit decodes the opcode in the instruction register and issues the control signals; the ALU only performs arithmetic and logic.

questions.q: Which bus carries signals such as READ, WRITE and interrupt acknowledge?
questions.exp: The control bus carries timing and control signals; the address bus (unidirectional) carries addresses, the data bus (bidirectional) carries data.

questions.q: The Harvard architecture, used by the 8051, PIC and AVR families, has
options: one common memory for program and data
separate memories and buses for program and data
only a cache and no main memory
questions.exp: Harvard architecture keeps program and data in separate memories, allowing simultaneous fetch of instruction and data; von Neumann uses a single memory.

questions.q: Which blocks are integrated on a single-chip microcontroller but are NOT part of the microprocessor (CPU) itself?
options: ROM/Flash, RAM, timers and I/O ports
questions.exp: A microcontroller = CPU + memory + peripherals on one chip; the microprocessor is only the CPU.

questions.q: Which hardware unit is used in embedded systems to reset the system automatically when the software hangs?
questions.exp: A watchdog timer must be refreshed periodically by software; if it times out, it resets the processor.

questions.q: Which memory type is commonly used to store firmware in modern microcontrollers and can be electrically erased block by block?
questions.exp: Flash is non-volatile and electrically erasable in blocks, so firmware can be updated in-system.

questions.q: After reset, the 8051 stack pointer and program counter contain
questions.exp: Reset sets PC = 0000H and SP = 07H, so the first PUSH stores data at 08H.

questions.q: Which bit position of the 8086 flag register holds the Overflow flag (OF)?
questions.exp: OF is bit D11; DF is D10, IF is D9 and SF is D7.

questions.q: An 8051 is driven by a 12 MHz crystal. The duration of one machine cycle is
questions.exp: One machine cycle = 12 oscillator periods = 12 / 12 MHz = 1 microsecond.

questions.q: In an 8086 program, AX = 0064H and BL = 07H. After DIV BL, the registers hold
questions.exp: 100 / 7 gives quotient 14 (0EH) in AL and remainder 2 in AH.

questions.q: Pins P3.2 and P3.3 of the 8051 have the alternate functions
questions.exp: P3.0 RXD, P3.1 TXD, P3.2 INT0, P3.3 INT1, P3.4 T0, P3.5 T1, P3.6 WR, P3.7 RD.

questions.q: The 8085 instruction RST 3 transfers control to which address?
questions.exp: RST n jumps to 8 x n; for n = 3 this is 18H.

questions.q: The 8085 status signal IO/M is HIGH during
options: an I/O read or write operation
a memory read or write operation
questions.exp: IO/M = 1 indicates an I/O operation and IO/M = 0 a memory operation.

questions.q: How many address lines are required to interface a 4K x 8 memory chip?
questions.exp: 4K = 4096 = 2^12 locations, so 12 address lines are needed.

questions.q: After executing XRA A in an 8085 program, the Zero and Carry flags are
questions.exp: A XOR A = 0, so Z = 1; XRA always clears CY.

questions.q: Which special function register of the 8051 holds the serial data for both transmission and reception?
questions.exp: SBUF is the serial buffer: writing sends data, reading gets received data (two physically separate registers at the same address).

questions.q: Setting the trap flag (TF) of the 8086 causes
options: a single-step interrupt after every instruction
questions.exp: With TF = 1 the processor generates a type-1 interrupt after each instruction, which is used for debugging.

questions.q:
Statement I: In I/O-mapped I/O the whole memory address space is available for memory.
Statement II: In I/O-mapped I/O arithmetic and logical instructions can be applied directly to I/O devices.
Which is correct?
questions.exp: I/O-mapped I/O uses a separate address space so memory is not reduced (I true), but only IN/OUT can access ports (II is a feature of memory-mapped I/O).
